# Meditate: full agent reference

Canonical docs: https://jmcentire.github.io/meditate/
Source: https://github.com/jmcentire/meditate
Version described: 0.2.0 alpha
Snapshot: 2026-08-19
License: MIT
Runtime: Python 3.11+

## First principle: authority before confidence

Operator instructions, explicit corrections, applicable scope, and named-actor handoff boundaries outrank model fluency, recency alone, evidence volume, and structural confidence. Temporal order informs an older record instead of deleting it. A newer record wins only when authority and scope permit it.

Meditate addresses monotonic append: after a correction, another exception is recorded without revising the rule that caused the failure. It is not a generic provider-state, vector-store, workspace, side-effect, cache, or model-weight scrubber.

## Objective and fixed point

The fixed point is stability. The objective is defect resolution, not size reduction. Objectives are ordered: correctness, checkability, scope precision, then concision. Byte and line counts are reported telemetry. Output may grow when a reason replaces brittle exception clauses; growth is still bounded by configured safety and consumer budgets but is not itself a defect.

Meditate MUST be idempotent: a well-formed instruction set must survive byte-identically. A no-op is a successful result. `stable_noop` means no local candidate existed; `reviewed_noop` means candidates were detected and reviewed but no admissible change was made. These states are intentionally distinct.

Preflight currently has one confirmed defect, `exact_duplicate`, and one review class, `exception_lineage`. Exception lineage requires exception-bearing directives in one heading with shared subject terms, but it is not proof that either directive is wrong. Density, age, history overlap, and byte count do not create defects.

With no candidate, `meditate plan` does not resolve provider credentials or instantiate a provider. It makes zero model calls, archives a successful byte-identical plan, and records `semantic_verification.status=not_applicable`.

When candidates exist, the provider receives the complete non-overlapping candidate set and only candidate directive IDs. Local code keeps unrelated records byte-for-byte. Each change remains inside one candidate, heading, and subject. After deterministic rendering, the entire post-image is segmented again. A changed plan that retains a confirmed defect fails `non_idempotent_proposal`; a review candidate may remain when kept.

Executable acceptance covers a well-formed unchanged fixture, a corrected defective fixture, a second invocation over both results with byte equality, ten iterations over the well-formed fixture without drift, one-pass convergence over a multi-defect fixture, and rejection of a partial multi-defect resolution.

## Authority and evidence

Default durable evidence order is: explicit user correction with an antecedent; current version-controlled instruction qualified by scope; repeated user preference across independent sessions; deterministic outcome evidence; active Kindex knowledge with provenance; agent auto-memory; assistant inference. Authority, semantic domain, scope, supersession, recency, and corroboration are separate dimensions. Retrieval relevance never creates authority.

Instruction files, histories, auto-memory, imports, and Kindex are read-only evidence. The tool writes only exact configured targets. If Kindex is enabled and `kin` is installed, all configured searches and requested node reads are mandatory. Any failure aborts before planning with `kindex_required_failed`; Meditate never silently creates a plan from partial durable evidence.

## Five total dispositions

Every source directive appears exactly once as keep, replace, remove, relocate, or escalate.

- keep copies source bytes unchanged.
- replace locally renders a typed compiled directive at the source location.
- remove deletes only with a cited ground: explicit supersession, an explicit resolved user decision, provably dead scope, or explicit user confirmation. A size quota is not a ground.
- relocate moves specific content to one exact configured target. Contextual relocation requires an exact configured `.claude/rules/` Markdown target with non-empty `paths:` frontmatter; Meditate never invents a glob.
- escalate is report-only. Source bytes remain unchanged while the report names a deterministic hook/settings candidate. It requires independent evidence groups and never installs enforcement.

Every change copies `destination_target` byte-for-byte from `allowed_targets`. Target strings are opaque. Replace, remove, and escalate use the exact source target; relocate selects another exact configured target. The model may not expand `~`, normalize, absolutize, or invent paths.

## Typed directive compilation and register

The provider cannot return free replacement Markdown. A semantic replacement supplies exactly:

- `normative_keyword`: `MUST`, `MUST NOT`, `SHOULD`, `SHOULD NOT`, or `MAY`, with RFC 2119 semantics;
- `rule`: concrete behavior, preferably naming a command, path, glob, or observable artifact;
- `reason`: the rationale that generates legitimate exceptions;
- `scope`: where the directive applies; and
- `boundary_example`: optional, only when one example materially pins the decision boundary.

Local code rejects missing or multiline fields, NULs, invalid keywords, embedded Markdown markers, and invented destinations, then renders canonical Markdown. `SHOULD` is a strong defeasible default, not decorative emphasis. A stated reason is compression when it replaces an expanding list of exceptions. A boundary example remains untrusted prose, not an executable test. The owner-authored suite is the behavior oracle.

Model-authored summaries are forbidden. Reports compute outcome, defect classes, disposition counts, and metrics locally from validated data. Repeated normalized eight-word phrases are rejected. Newly introduced unsupported catch-alls such as `other applicable actions`, `additional applicable actions`, `and similar`, `etc`, and `and so on` are rejected unless that exact catch-all already exists in source or cited evidence.

## Planner-blind behavioral qualification

Structural validation is not behavioral qualification. Every changed plan records `semantic_verification.status=required` with method `owner_defined_hidden_detector_suite_v2`. A no-change plan records `not_applicable`.

`meditate verify RUN_ID` loads an owner-authored JSON suite from an explicit path or config. The planner never receives the suite or verifier outcomes. Each case runs in three conditions: control with no project/user instruction file, the complete archived predecessor bundle, and the complete candidate bundle. The configured Claude or Codex consumer CLI repeats the matrix, sees only neutral scenarios and opaque case references, and returns free-form ordered plans naming concrete tools or commands. Semantic case IDs, action IDs, detector phrases, and required/forbidden/order assertions never cross that model boundary. Bounded private local literal detectors derive actions after generation; local code then enforces required, forbidden, and ordered behavior. A candidate must pass every case on every repeat, must not regress below its predecessor on any case, and must strictly outperform each designated control. Predecessor misses are reported as `baseline_gap_cases`; repaired misses are reported as `candidate_improvement_cases`. A baseline gap cannot excuse a candidate miss or veto an all-green, non-regressing candidate.

Every changed source directive needs suite coverage. The immutable receipt binds the suite bytes/hash loaded before execution, plan hash, pre/post target hashes, evaluation prompt and response-schema hashes, each condition's complete system-prompt hash, consumer agent and CLI version, requested/resolved model, repeat count, responses, response hashes, and case outcomes. Apply independently reconstructs the prompt/schema/system bindings and fails if the receipt is absent, failed, stale, or for another plan/target/suite.

A passed receipt proves only the owner-selected cases on the recorded consumer agent/version/model. It is not universal behavioral equivalence, does not validate uncovered behaviors, and does not attest that the planner selected a good defect. The planner cannot see or write the oracle.

Codex verification creates a fresh private `CODEX_HOME`, ignores ambient user config and rules, and requires `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Its control therefore cannot inherit global `AGENTS.md`, memories, or user configuration. Anthropic planning uses `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Credential values are not persisted.

Unattended apply is a separate authority gate. Besides a passed receipt it requires explicit configuration, attended probation history, and a low-blast-radius plan. A semantic pass does not authorize protected changes, remote actions, or an otherwise forbidden mutation.

### v0.2.0 live qualification receipts

The restored live Claude and Codex targets produced zero-call, byte-identical `stable_noop` runs `20260819T161206Z-d6dbad85` and `20260819T161218Z-834d615b`. Their SHA-256 values remained `441fe6e9af0302329b753fa9138f6a5fc5c556637991bfec679700adea1acb76` and `0dd415bb140f10fe95c70005e33ca523f1ed60419a79bbfeabdf9a31446c6b63`.

Disposable Claude plan `20260819T165955Z-1987f9ef` resolved one exact duplicate, moving from 67 directives/11,606 bytes to 66 directives/11,378 bytes. Claude Code 2.1.224 with `claude-sonnet-4-6` scored pre 18/18, post 18/18, and control 0/18. Verification SHA `4f1851d08ddb4047243f6978204bda6b29ad59d245dd744a020e31321eb878aa` authorized attended apply only to the disposable copy. Second run `20260819T170602Z-39e3bba4` was a zero-call byte-identical no-op.

Claude run `20260819T165129Z-70f323ea` scored pre 18/18 and post 17/18 after a lower-position rewrite. It failed closed and was never applied, demonstrating that smaller or coherent output does not bypass the behavioral gate.

Disposable Codex plan `20260819T171655Z-546b02cd` resolved one exact duplicate, moving from 35 directives/5,269 bytes to 34 directives/4,830 bytes. Codex CLI 0.147.0 with `gpt-5.6-sol` in a fresh private `CODEX_HOME` scored post 18/18 and control 0/18. One predecessor repeat miss was repaired and appears as both a baseline gap and candidate improvement. Verification SHA `0376960893146c8f9f29559da0fee2a9f14a0b182eae3759689dda2b0e915b1d` authorized attended apply only to the disposable copy. Second run `20260819T171954Z-d68b18c5` was a zero-call byte-identical no-op.

These receipts cover six owner-authored Kindex cases on the named consumer versions and models only. They are not universal behavioral equivalence or a promise about future models.

## Workflow order and enforcement

Operational action lists establish coverage, not universal order. A high-impact proposal must follow the exact loaded repository workflow. Before an action it may require only checks that are applicable, project-required, and available before that action. Push-, PR-, and merge-triggered CI, approvals, and named handoffs are evaluated at their own stages. Requiring all CI before commit is invalid.

Instructions are probabilistic context. Deterministic, fixed-lifecycle, zero-judgment rules belong in hooks, permissions, exec policy, settings, linters, or CI. Escalation identifies these candidates but does not promise equivalent enforcement across agents: Claude hooks and Codex controls have different interception limits.

## Bounded operator decisions

`decision_request` is null unless a genuine, materially behavior-changing authority collision remains between at least two preserved directives and authority, scope, or time cannot decide it. Competing evidence must have equal authority, equal scope, and the same timestamp. Older evidence remains lineage rather than an equal choice. Mere ambiguity preserves current prose and blocks.

The model provides two subjects and exactly three evidence-grounded options. It puts its advisory recommendation first but cannot answer, select, mint keys/IDs, or create the custom escape. Local code assigns a/b/c, marks only a as recommended, adds custom, and derives stable fingerprints and IDs. Display fields are bounded and single-line.

Rendered question: `I’m trying to resolve {subject_a} and {subject_b}. Would you prefer {A} (recommended), {B}, {C}, or something else?`

The framing and recommendation are model-authored, untrusted, and advisory. `meditate decisions RUN_ID` instructs an invoking agent to relay the question, not execute a recommendation. `meditate decide RUN_ID REQUEST_ID --choice a|b|c` or `--custom TEXT` records operator-asserted user authority and creates a fresh read-only successor from frozen parent evidence. Identity is not authenticated or attested, and the process cannot prove an agent faithfully relayed the user’s answer. A decision cannot bypass protected directives or higher authority.

## Claude imports, scope, and budgets

Configured writable roots named `CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md` recursively parse official `@path` imports outside code spans/fences. Relative, absolute, and `~/` imports are supported to four hops. Dangling, circular, over-depth, non-regular, and non-UTF-8 imports fail. Graph nodes, hashes, edges, and a digest are bound before and after planning and apply.

Operators must trust configured Claude roots and import graphs: an import may read any process-readable file it names. Import-only documents are sanitized immutable context and cannot be written through their import role. Recognized secret shapes are redacted locally, but pattern redaction is not a filesystem sandbox or comprehensive secret detector. Same-user filesystem compromise is outside Meditate’s threat boundary.

A Claude `CLAUDE.md` post-state over 200 lines is a guidance status, not a represented vendor hard limit. Meditate reads Codex `project_doc_max_bytes` when available and otherwise uses 32,768 bytes. It checks the configured writable `AGENTS*.md` target set with coverage `configured_targets_only`; passing does not prove every cwd-specific concatenated chain fits.

## Provenance, recovery, and privacy

Plans bind schema version, requested model, API-returned resolved model ID, prompt version/hash, parser version, exact operations, semantic status, target/import hashes, and metrics. Prompt version 10 uses SHA-256 `d277c05dee519d697586dcf3a1cdf74c3a848ee2297e83985d7c96b66ff50d72`; parser version is `meditate-parser-v25`.

Apply verifies immutable archives, current config/source/import hashes, plan approval, and any required semantic receipt. It refuses symlinks, writes same-directory temporary files, preserves modes, fsyncs, atomically replaces, and rolls back earlier targets if a later write fails. Restore refuses later hand-edit drift unless forced; forced restore first archives the diverged bytes.

`inspect` is local-only. A stable no-op makes zero provider calls. `plan` sends only candidate directives, bounded immutable context, and selected locally secret-scanned/redacted evidence to Anthropic. `verify` separately sends owner probe text and full pre/post instruction bundles to the configured Claude or Codex CLI, which may transmit them to its provider. The planner never receives the suite. Private artifacts live in XDG data/state directories. There is no product telemetry.

Runtime credentials use only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for planning and `OPENAI_API_KEY` for clean-room Codex verification. Credential values are never written to plans, reports, archives, or release artifacts.

## Commands

- `meditate init`: write commented TOML configuration.
- `meditate inspect [--json]`: local inventory, imports, metrics, and overlap candidates; no model call or target mutation.
- `meditate plan [planning flags]`: return a zero-call no-op or create, validate, archive, and report a typed proposal.
- `meditate verify RUN_ID --suite FILE --agent claude|codex [--model ID] [--repeats N]`: run and bind the planner-blind consumer suite.
- `meditate decisions RUN_ID [--json]`: show one pending bounded authority question.
- `meditate decide RUN_ID REQUEST_ID (--choice a|b|c | --custom TEXT)`: create a frozen-context successor plan.
- `meditate apply RUN_ID (--approve PLAN_SHA256 | --unattended)`: revalidate and atomically apply an eligible archived plan.
- `meditate restore RUN_ID [--force] [--recover]`: restore exact pre-images under drift rules.
- `meditate run [planning flags] [--apply]`: inspect, plan, optionally verify, then enter normal unattended gates.
- `meditate cron [--check] [--schedule CRON] [--apply]`: print or validate a locked invocation; never edit crontab.
- `meditate purge RUN_ID [--execute] [--force]`: preview or explicitly erase a named archive with replay-safe markers.

## Distribution

The canonical public distribution for v0.2.0 is the GitHub Release wheel:
https://github.com/jmcentire/meditate/releases/download/v0.2.0/meditate_agent-0.2.0-py3-none-any.whl

PyPI publication is not claimed. CI validates Ruff, strict mypy, pytest on supported Python versions, and an isolated wheel build but does not publish.

## Why not a linter?

Adjacent tools already provide static instruction-health checks and fixes. Meditate’s narrower distinction is defect-grounded total disposition, temporal evidence, typed directive compilation, independent consumer-agent qualification, and content-addressed recoverable apply. It does not claim those tools do nothing.

The exact purported title `A Taxonomy of Agent Instruction Failures` by Gloaguen et al. was not verified and is not load-bearing. The verified paper is `Coding Agents Don't Know When to Act`: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07769.
